### REQ-018: Move status reporting out of the FreeRTOS timer daemon task

- **Status:** DONE
- **Added:** 2026-07-02
- **Completed:** 2026-07-04
- **Verified by:** code review + idf.py build 2026-07-04 (status timer deleted, tick-counted report in control task; soak test pending, no board attached)
- **Depends on:** REQ-009, REQ-010
- **Description:**

`statusReportCallback` (`main.cpp:331-338, 488-496`) runs `thermoInstance->sendStatus()` in the FreeRTOS timer service task, whose stack is only `CONFIG_FREERTOS_TIMER_TASK_STACK_DEPTH = 3072` bytes. `sendStatus()` builds ArduinoJson documents, serializes `std::string`s and performs MQTT publishes for the device plus every room — marginal stack headroom, and any growth (more rooms, longer names) risks a daemon-task stack overflow (crash). MQTT publishing also blocks the daemon, delaying every other software timer.

Fix: the timer callback should only signal (task notification / event bit / queue item) a normal task — e.g. the control task checks the flag in `updateControl()`, or a small dedicated reporter task performs `sendStatus()`. Alternatively (stopgap only) raise the timer stack to ≥ 6144.

Side effect to fix at the same time: `Thermo::getStatusJsonAsObj()` reports `uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark(nullptr)` (`core/thermo.cpp:149`), which measures whatever task happens to run it — make `freeStack` report a named task (or the minimum across app tasks) so the telemetry is meaningful.

See finding F-6 in `doc/reports/2026-07-02_migration_code_review.md`.

- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - [x] No JSON serialization or MQTT publish executes in the timer service task (code inspection — the xTimer was deleted entirely; reporting is tick-counted in the control task)
  - [ ] 60 s status reports still delivered; skipped cleanly when MQTT disconnected — *pending on-device check, no board attached 2026-07-04*
  - [ ] Timer daemon high-water mark stable over 24 h soak — *pending, no board attached 2026-07-04*
  - [x] `freeStack` status field documents which stack it reports (control task; comment at `core/thermo.cpp` getStatusJsonAsObj)
- **Notes:** Combines naturally with REQ-019 (reporting cadence), since both touch how/where status reports are triggered.
